articles.author: Declan
articles.description:
When merging CSVs in the browser, handling mismatched columns and quoted cells changes everything. Here's how filetools does it.
Last week we shipped CSV merge/split/transpose tools for filetools, and the most interesting challenge wasn't CSV parsing - it was handling real-world data without a server. Here's how we handle the hard cases.
The Problem:
CSV files in the wild are messy. Columns don't always match. A cell value contains a comma and that comma is quoted. Headers are sometimes case-sensitive, sometimes not. When you build on a server, you can run a fast library and stream the result. In the browser, you have to make your merge operation deterministic from first load.
Our approach:
Column matching: Users specify which columns to merge on (e.g., "id" or "email"). We do a case-insen…
articles.title: How We Handle Client-Side CSV Merging Without Server Processing

articles.author: Matheus de Camargo Marques
articles.description:
Todo mundo que começa a explorar as ferramentas de Inteligência Artificial acaba esbarrando na mesma ideia: "vou abrir uma loja virtual" ou "vou criar um SaaS". A IA derrubou as barreiras técnicas. Hoje, qualquer pessoa consegue gerar a marca, o site e o código de um e-commerce em minutos.
Mas quem realmente está ganhando a "Corrida do Ouro" da IA?
Na corrida do ouro americana, quem ficou rico não foram os garimpeiros, mas sim quem vendia as pás e picaretas. No cenário atual, as pás e picaretas são os Meios de Pagamento (Stripe, Mercado Pago, PayPal).
Eles não precisam que a sua loja virtual seja um unicórnio. Para a infraestrutura de pagamentos, não importa se o seu projeto de IA vai faturar milhões ou falir em dois meses. O modelo de negócio deles lucra na volumetria. A IA inundou a internet com novos projetos, e absolutamente todos eles desaguam no mesmo gargalo: o checkout.
Até as próprias gigantes (OpenAI, Midjourney) pagam o "pedágio" dessa infraestrutura para processar as assinaturas.
A revolução da IA é real, mas os maiores beneficiários silenciosos dela são os donos do asfalto por onde todo o dinheiro da internet precisa passar.
E você, de qual lado dessa corrida do ouro está construindo?
articles.title: A IA é um "esquema de pirâmide" para os meios de pagamento?

There are now tens of thousands of MCP servers. Glama indexes ~75,000. PulseMCP lists ~22,000. npm has thousands of packages tagged mcp-server. And yet the way we all use MCP is: find a server somewhere, paste it into a config file, restart the client, repeat.
Your agent can't answer "is there a tool that queries Postgres?" — you have to know the answer, find the server, and wire it up before the conversation even starts.
mcp-anything is a single MCP server that inverts this. Instead of you configuring N servers, the model gets exactly five meta-tools:
search_mcp_servers   → BM25 search over the indexed ecosystem
​
The index is built by syncing four catalogs — the official MCP registry, PulseMCP, npm search, and Glama — deduplicating across them by normalized repository URL and package ide…

Every browser testing comparison eventually collapses into a speed argument, and that framing hides the thing that actually matters. Cypress is not Selenium with the rough edges sanded off. It made one architectural decision that pays for most of its strengths and every one of its limits, and once you see that decision clearly, choosing between it and Playwright stops being a matter of taste.
Selenium and the tools built on WebDriver sit outside the browser. A command leaves the test process, travels to a driver binary, gets translated into a protocol message, and only then reaches the DOM. Every one of those boundaries adds latency and creates a place where things break for reasons that have nothing to do with the application.
